q: Air, water and soil are three ____ that we cannot live without.
e: Air, water and soil are three natural resources that we cannot live without. Natural resources is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The earth is surrounded by a layer of air about 8~10 km thick called the ____.
e: The earth is surrounded by a layer of air about 8~10 km thick called the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of air around Earth, split into troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere.

q: The atmosphere is divided into four layers: ____, stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere.
e: The atmosphere is divided into four layers: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere. The troposphere is the lowest layer, where almost all weather and living things are. The atmosphere is the layer of air around Earth, split into troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere.

q: About 75% of the mass of the atmosphere is found in the layer nearest the Earth called the ____.
e: About 75% of the mass of the atmosphere is found in the layer nearest the Earth called the troposphere. The troposphere is the lowest layer, where almost all weather and living things are.

q: The next region, ____, is where we find the ozone layer that shields living creatures from deadly ultraviolet radiation.
e: The next region, stratosphere, is where we find the ozone layer that shields living creatures from deadly ultraviolet radiation. The stratosphere holds the ozone layer that screens much UV light.

q: Dry air contains (by volume) 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen ($O_2$), 0.03% ____ ($CO_2$) and 0.97% noble gases.
e: Dry air contains (by volume) 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen (O2), 0.03% carbon dioxide (CO2) and 0.97% noble gases. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased from 0.03% to its present value ____.
e: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased from 0.03% to its present value 0.04%. 0.04% is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The amount of water vapour in air can vary widely around the world, from almost 0% in a desert to about ____ in a tropical forest.
e: The amount of water vapour in air can vary widely around the world, from almost 0% in a desert to about 5% in a tropical forest. 5% is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is the reactive part of the air.
e: Oxygen is the reactive part of the air. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal.

q: The three important reactions involving oxygen are combustion, ____ and rusting.
e: The three important reactions involving oxygen are combustion, respiration and rusting. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal.

q: The process for respiration goes on in all our cells, by taking oxygen and releasing ____ and water.
e: The process for respiration goes on in all our cells, by taking oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide and water. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Green plants need carbon dioxide for ____ to produce glucose and oxygen.
e: Green plants need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen. Photosynthesis uses chlorophyll to trap light and build sugar from carbon dioxide and water.

q: The gases in air can be separated from each other by ____.
e: The gases in air can be separated from each other by fractional distillation. Distillation separates liquids by boiling point, then condenses the vapour.

q: In the separation of gases from air, air is pumped into the plant and filtered to remove ____.
e: In the separation of gases from air, air is pumped into the plant and filtered to remove dust particles. Dust particles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Carbon dioxide, water vapour and pollutants are removed since these would freeze later and ____.
e: Carbon dioxide, water vapour and pollutants are removed since these would freeze later and block the pipes. Block the pipes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: At ____, air becomes liquid (liquefaction), except neon and helium.
e: At -200℃, air becomes liquid (liquefaction), except neon and helium. -200℃ is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The liquid air is pumped into the ____ and it is slowly warmed up.
e: The liquid air is pumped into the fractionating column and it is slowly warmed up. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points.

q: In the fractional distillation of liquid air, ____ with the lowest boiling point boils off first.
e: In the fractional distillation of liquid air, Nitrogen with the lowest boiling point boils off first. Nitrogen is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are six main air pollutants: carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, ____, methane, unburnt hydrocarbons and ozone.
e: There are six main air pollutants: carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, methane, unburnt hydrocarbons and ozone. Nitrogen dioxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Carbon monoxide is formed by the incomplete combustion of ____ substances.
e: Carbon monoxide is formed by the incomplete combustion of carbon-containing substances. Carbon-containing is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Carbon monoxide reacts with the ____ in blood and prevents it from carrying oxygen around the body.
e: Carbon monoxide reacts with the haemoglobin in blood and prevents it from carrying oxygen around the body. Haemoglobin is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sulphur dioxide is produced by the combustion of ____ in motor vehicles, power stations and factories.
e: Sulphur dioxide is produced by the combustion of fossil fuels in motor vehicles, power stations and factories. Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum, and natural gas, formed from ancient remains and finite. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning.

q: Nitrogen dioxide is an acidic gas produced by vehicle exhaust fumes, chemical plants and ____.
e: Nitrogen dioxide is an acidic gas produced by vehicle exhaust fumes, chemical plants and lightning activity. Lightning activity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Methane is a colourless gas with no smell that causes ____ because it is a greenhouse gas.
e: Methane is a colourless gas with no smell that causes global warming because it is a greenhouse gas. Global warming is the rise in Earth's average temperature from extra greenhouse gases.

q: Unburnt hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust fumes and chemical plants can cause ____.
e: Unburnt hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust fumes and chemical plants can cause cancer. Cancer is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ozone is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons in the presence of ____.
e: Ozone is formed by the reaction of nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons in the presence of sunlight. Sunlight is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The Earth's surface releases heat in the form of ____ radiation.
e: The Earth's surface releases heat in the form of infrared radiation. Infrared is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Carbon dioxide and other gases in the air trap infrared radiation and prevent much of it escaping into ____.
e: Carbon dioxide and other gases in the air trap infrared radiation and prevent much of it escaping into space. Space is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The gases that occur naturally in the atmosphere and trap heat are called ____.
e: The gases that occur naturally in the atmosphere and trap heat are called greenhouse gases. Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat in the atmosphere.

q: Man-made chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), and ____ are also greenhouse gases.
e: Man-made chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), and sulphur hexafluoride are also greenhouse gases. Sulphur hexafluoride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Human activities such as burning fossil fuels and excessive use of ____ increase the amount of greenhouse gases.
e: Human activities such as burning fossil fuels and excessive use of fertilisers increase the amount of greenhouse gases. Fertilisers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The melting of glaciers and Arctic ice will increase ____ resulting in many coastal communities being flooded.
e: The melting of glaciers and Arctic ice will increase sea levels resulting in many coastal communities being flooded. Sea levels is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Rain water is naturally slightly acidic (pH of about ____) because carbon dioxide in the air dissolves in it to form carbonic acid.
e: Rain water is naturally slightly acidic (pH of about 5.7) because carbon dioxide in the air dissolves in it to form carbonic acid. 5.7 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When oxides of sulphur and nitrogen dissolve in water, water becomes more ____.
e: When oxides of sulphur and nitrogen dissolve in water, water becomes more acidic. Acidic oxides are usually non-metal oxides that make acids with water or react with bases.

q: Sulphur dioxide reacts with oxygen and water to form ____.
e: Sulphur dioxide reacts with oxygen and water to form sulphuric acid. Sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen dioxide reacts with oxygen and water to form ____.
e: Nitrogen dioxide reacts with oxygen and water to form nitric acid. Nitric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Rain water with a pH less than ____ is called acid rain.
e: Rain water with a pH less than 5 is called acid rain. 5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Acid rain has many negative effects, including killing animals and plant life, and damaging metal bridges and ____.
e: Acid rain has many negative effects, including killing animals and plant life, and damaging metal bridges and stone buildings. Stone buildings is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen is flushed through food packaging to remove oxygen and keep the food ____.
e: Nitrogen is flushed through food packaging to remove oxygen and keep the food fresh. Fresh is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Liquid nitrogen (bpt. -196℃) is used to quick-freeze food and to store ____ in hospitals.
e: Liquid nitrogen (bpt. -196℃) is used to quick-freeze food and to store tissue samples in hospitals. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together.

q: Nitrogen is used with argon to fill electric bulbs because these gases do not react with ____.
e: Nitrogen is used with argon to fill electric bulbs because these gases do not react with tungsten filament. Tungsten filament is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Carbon dioxide is used widely as a coolant, a refrigerant, an ingredient in frozen foods, and as a ____.
e: Carbon dioxide is used widely as a coolant, a refrigerant, an ingredient in frozen foods, and as a fire extinguisher. Fire extinguisher is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ provides the inert atmosphere in ordinary tungsten light bulbs.
e: Argon provides the inert atmosphere in ordinary tungsten light bulbs. Argon is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Neon is used in advertising signs because it glows ____ when a current is passed through it.
e: Neon is used in advertising signs because it glows red when a current is passed through it. Red is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water is the ____ compound on this planet.
e: Water is the commonest compound on this planet. Commonest is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Human bones contain ____ water, kidneys are about 82% water and blood is about 90% water.
e: Human bones contain 31% water, kidneys are about 82% water and blood is about 90% water. 31% is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Out of 100% of water that covers the Earth's surface, 97.5% is sea water; only ____ make up fresh water.
e: Out of 100% of water that covers the Earth's surface, 97.5% is sea water; only 2.5% make up fresh water. 2.5% is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Out of 2.5% fresh water, 1.97% make up ice caps and glaciers, 0.5% make up ____, only 0.02% make up lakes and rivers.
e: Out of 2.5% fresh water, 1.97% make up ice caps and glaciers, 0.5% make up ground water, only 0.02% make up lakes and rivers. Ground water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ water cannot be found in nature.
e: Pure water cannot be found in nature. Pure is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is the purest form of natural water.
e: Rain water is the purest form of natural water. Rain water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Dissolved ____ makes rain water slightly acidic.
e: Dissolved carbon dioxide makes rain water slightly acidic. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: River water contains some dissolved gases and also some dissolved ____ depending upon the soil over which it passes.
e: River water contains some dissolved gases and also some dissolved solids depending upon the soil over which it passes. Solids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sea water contains various soluble salts (about ____).
e: Sea water contains various soluble salts (about 3.5%). 3.5% is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pure water is a clear, transparent and ____ liquid in thin layers.
e: Pure water is a clear, transparent and colourless liquid in thin layers. Colourless is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water has a greater ____ than almost any other liquid.
e: Water has a greater specific heat capacity than almost any other liquid. Specific heat capacity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water has the very unusual property of having a maximum density at a temperature of ____ to the nearest degree.
e: Water has the very unusual property of having a maximum density at a temperature of 4℃ to the nearest degree. 4℃ is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water is regarded as the most ____ because it dissolves almost all substances to a greater or lesser extent.
e: Water is regarded as the most universal solvent because it dissolves almost all substances to a greater or lesser extent. The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving, often water.

q: A small fraction of dissolved carbon dioxide reacts with water to produce ____, which is a weak acid.
e: A small fraction of dissolved carbon dioxide reacts with water to produce carbonic acid, which is a weak acid. Carbonic acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The weak acid in rain attacks rocks containing limestone (calcium carbonate, $CaCO_3$) and ____ (calcium magnesium carbonate, $CaMg(CO_3)_2$).
e: The weak acid in rain attacks rocks containing limestone (calcium carbonate, CaCO3) and dolomite (calcium magnesium carbonate, CaMg(CO3)2). Dolomite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The presence of dissolved sulphates or ____ causes the water to become 'hard'.
e: The presence of dissolved sulphates or hydrogen carbonates causes the water to become 'hard'. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: Soap is the sodium salt of ____.
e: Soap is the sodium salt of organic fatty acid. Organic fatty acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The most common soap is sodium stearate, which is the sodium salt of ____.
e: The most common soap is sodium stearate, which is the sodium salt of stearic acid. Stearic acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Detergents contain molecules with a salt-like group attached to a long chain of ____.
e: Detergents contain molecules with a salt-like group attached to a long chain of hydrocarbon. A hydrocarbon contains only hydrogen and carbon.

q: Sodium alkyl benzene sulphonates are synthetic ____.
e: Sodium alkyl benzene sulphonates are synthetic soapless detergents. Soapless detergents is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In hard water areas, it is difficult to make the soap ____.
e: In hard water areas, it is difficult to make the soap lather. Lather is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The white solid material formed by the reaction of dissolved substances in hard water with soap is known as ____.
e: The white solid material formed by the reaction of dissolved substances in hard water with soap is known as scum. Scum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sodium stearate reacts with calcium hydrogen carbonate to form calcium stearate (scum) and ____.
e: Sodium stearate reacts with calcium hydrogen carbonate to form calcium stearate (scum) and sodium hydrogen carbonate. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: To overcome the problem of scum formation, ____ have been developed.
e: To overcome the problem of scum formation, soapless detergents have been developed. Soapless detergents is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Degree of hardness of water is defined as the number of parts of mass of ____ ($CaCO_3$), equivalent to various calcium and magnesium salts present in one million parts by mass of water.
e: Degree of hardness of water is defined as the number of parts of mass of calcium carbonate (CaCO3), equivalent to various calcium and magnesium salts present in one million parts by mass of water. Calcium carbonate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in ____ (parts per million).
e: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in ppm (parts per million). Ppm is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water with a degree of hardness of less than 17.1 mg/L is classified as ____.
e: Water with a degree of hardness of less than 17.1 mg/L is classified as soft. Soft water has few calcium and magnesium ions, so soap lathers easily.

q: Water with a degree of hardness of 17.1~60 mg/L is classified as ____.
e: Water with a degree of hardness of 17.1~60 mg/L is classified as slightly hard. Slightly hard is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water with a degree of hardness of 60~120 mg/L is classified as ____.
e: Water with a degree of hardness of 60~120 mg/L is classified as moderately hard. Moderately hard is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water with a degree of hardness greater than 180 mg/L is classified as ____.
e: Water with a degree of hardness greater than 180 mg/L is classified as very hard. Very hard is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Temporary hardness is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium or magnesium ____.
e: Temporary hardness is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium or magnesium hydrogen carbonates. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: Temporary hardness is so called because it is easily removed by ____.
e: Temporary hardness is so called because it is easily removed by boiling. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: Permanent hardness is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium or magnesium chlorides and ____.
e: Permanent hardness is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium or magnesium chlorides and sulphates. Sulphates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When hard water is evaporated, a white solid deposit of calcium or magnesium sulphate and/or calcium carbonate, known as ____, is left behind.
e: When hard water is evaporated, a white solid deposit of calcium or magnesium sulphate and/or calcium carbonate, known as limescale, is left behind. Limescale is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Calcium carbonate is formed from the decomposition of ____ by heating.
e: Calcium carbonate is formed from the decomposition of calcium hydrogen carbonate by heating. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: The furring of kettles caused by calcium carbonate may be removed by the addition of ____.
e: The furring of kettles caused by calcium carbonate may be removed by the addition of dilute acid. Dilute acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The calcium or magnesium ion, which causes hardness, is removed as a precipitate by adding ____.
e: The calcium or magnesium ion, which causes hardness, is removed as a precipitate by adding washing soda. Washing soda is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main causes of water pollution are sewage, fertilisers, pesticides, industrial wastes, oil and ____.
e: The main causes of water pollution are sewage, fertilisers, pesticides, industrial wastes, oil and detergents. Detergents is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Industrial waste containing heavy metals such as Pb, Cu, Cd, Hg, Cr, etc. causes ____.
e: Industrial waste containing heavy metals such as Pb, Cu, Cd, Hg, Cr, etc. causes chronic health problems. Chronic health problems is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pesticides from agriculture fields are poisonous and can cause problems ranging from respiratory issues to ____.
e: Pesticides from agriculture fields are poisonous and can cause problems ranging from respiratory issues to cancer. Cancer is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fertilisers from agriculture fields cause waterway pollution, chemical burns to crops, increased air pollution, and ____ of the soil.
e: Fertilisers from agriculture fields cause waterway pollution, chemical burns to crops, increased air pollution, and mineral depletion of the soil. Mineral depletion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Oil spills from oil tankers seriously affect the ____.
e: Oil spills from oil tankers seriously affect the marine environment. Marine environment is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Polluted water can be purified by several methods such as filtration, chlorination, distillation and ____.
e: Polluted water can be purified by several methods such as filtration, chlorination, distillation and deionisation. Deionisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ionic impurities can be effectively and cheaply removed from water by passing through substances like ____ having a giant structure.
e: Ionic impurities can be effectively and cheaply removed from water by passing through substances like zeolite having a giant structure. Zeolite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A zeolite is an aluminosilicate, also known as ____.
e: A zeolite is an aluminosilicate, also known as sodium aluminium silicate. Sodium aluminium silicate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In zeolite, sodium ions are loosely held and may be replaced by ions of calcium, magnesium and ____ present in hard water.
e: In zeolite, sodium ions are loosely held and may be replaced by ions of calcium, magnesium and iron present in hard water. Iron is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The removal of calcium, magnesium and iron by zeolite results in the removal of hardness according to the ____ method.
e: The removal of calcium, magnesium and iron by zeolite results in the removal of hardness according to the Permutit method. Permutit is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the Permutit method, sodium zeolite reacts with calcium chloride to form calcium zeolite and ____.
e: In the Permutit method, sodium zeolite reacts with calcium chloride to form calcium zeolite and sodium chloride. Sodium chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water is used for cooking, cleaning, drinking, gardening and ____ (toilet flushing) in the home.
e: Water is used for cooking, cleaning, drinking, gardening and waste disposal (toilet flushing) in the home. Waste disposal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In industry, water is applied as a solvent, cleansing agent, coolant, major ingredient, and for ____.
e: In industry, water is applied as a solvent, cleansing agent, coolant, major ingredient, and for generating electricity. Generating electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Like air and water, ____ plays an essential role in our ecosystems.
e: Like air and water, soil plays an essential role in our ecosystems. Soil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Earth's body of soil, called the ____, has four important functions including being a medium for plant growth and a habitat for organisms.
e: Earth's body of soil, called the pedosphere, has four important functions including being a medium for plant growth and a habitat for organisms. Pedosphere is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is the upper layer of the Earth in which plants grow, typically consisting of a mixture of organic remains, clay and ____.
e: Soil is the upper layer of the Earth in which plants grow, typically consisting of a mixture of organic remains, clay and rock particles. Rock particles is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The three main layers of the soil with increasing depth are top soil, subsoil and ____.
e: The three main layers of the soil with increasing depth are top soil, subsoil and bedrock. Bedrock is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The sequence of the soil layers with increasing depth is called the ____.
e: The sequence of the soil layers with increasing depth is called the soil profile. Soil profile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The top layer of soil is known as the top soil or the ____ layer, which is rich in organic materials.
e: The top layer of soil is known as the top soil or the humus layer, which is rich in organic materials. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The top soil has a dark brown colour because it consists of decomposed material and ____.
e: The top soil has a dark brown colour because it consists of decomposed material and organic matter. Organic matter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The humus makes the top soil soft and ____ to hold enough air and water.
e: The humus makes the top soil soft and porous to hold enough air and water. Porous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the top soil layer, the seeds ____ and roots of the plants grow.
e: In the top soil layer, the seeds germinate and roots of the plants grow. Germinate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many living organisms like ____, bacteria and fungi are found in the top soil layer.
e: Many living organisms like earthworms, bacteria and fungi are found in the top soil layer. Earthworms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Just below the top soil lies another layer called ____.
e: Just below the top soil lies another layer called subsoil. Subsoil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is comparatively harder and more ____ than top soil.
e: The subsoil is comparatively harder and more compact than top soil. Compact is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is lighter in colour than the top soil because there is less ____ in this layer.
e: The subsoil is lighter in colour than the top soil because there is less humus in this layer. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil is less organic but is rich in ____ brought down from the top soil.
e: The subsoil is less organic but is rich in minerals brought down from the top soil. Minerals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The subsoil contains metal salts, especially ____ in a large proportion.
e: The subsoil contains metal salts, especially iron oxide in a large proportion. Iron oxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The next layer is bedrock or ____, which lies just below the subsoil.
e: The next layer is bedrock or parent rock, which lies just below the subsoil. Parent rock is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bedrock contains no ____ and is made up of stones and rocks, so it is very hard.
e: Bedrock contains no organic matter and is made up of stones and rocks, so it is very hard. Organic matter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mineral component of soil originates from the parent rocks by ____ processes.
e: The mineral component of soil originates from the parent rocks by weathering processes. Weathering is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The basic components of soil are mineral matter (45%), organic matter (5%), air (20~30%) and ____.
e: The basic components of soil are mineral matter (45%), organic matter (5%), air (20~30%) and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Air and water occupy the ____ in soils.
e: Air and water occupy the pore spaces in soils. Pore spaces is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pore spaces are the ____ between the soil particles.
e: Pore spaces are the voids between the soil particles. Voids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fine-textured soils have more total ____ than coarse-textured soils.
e: Fine-textured soils have more total pore space than coarse-textured soils. Pore space is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As soils absorb water, the ____ decreases.
e: As soils absorb water, the air space decreases. Air space is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Except for gravel and rocks, the three fractions of soil are sand, silt and ____.
e: Except for gravel and rocks, the three fractions of soil are sand, silt and clay. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The organic matter of soils is made up of undecomposed and partially decomposed residues of plants and animals and the tissue of living and dead ____.
e: The organic matter of soils is made up of undecomposed and partially decomposed residues of plants and animals and the tissue of living and dead microorganisms. Microorganisms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil texture is characterised by the relative proportion of sand, silt and ____ separates found in the soil.
e: Soil texture is characterised by the relative proportion of sand, silt and clay separates found in the soil. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A coarse sand will feel gritty but a wet clay will feel heavy and ____.
e: A coarse sand will feel gritty but a wet clay will feel heavy and sticky. Sticky is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is made up of different-sized particles, and ____ particles tend to be the biggest.
e: Soil is made up of different-sized particles, and sand particles tend to be the biggest. Sand is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ particles are very small.
e: Clay particles are very small. Clay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the proportion of sand in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes ____ in texture.
e: If the proportion of sand in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes coarser in texture. Coarser is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the proportion of clay in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes ____ in texture.
e: If the proportion of clay in the soil is increased, the resultant soil becomes finer in texture. Finer is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The soil textural triangle is a classification system used to determine soil classes based on their ____.
e: The soil textural triangle is a classification system used to determine soil classes based on their physical texture. Physical texture is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are ____ classes of soil texture as shown in the soil textural triangle.
e: There are twelve classes of soil texture as shown in the soil textural triangle. Twelve is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The term ____ refers to a soil with a combination of sand, silt and clay sized particles.
e: The term loam refers to a soil with a combination of sand, silt and clay sized particles. Loam is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand and 20% silt is called a ____.
e: A soil with 30% clay, 50% sand and 20% silt is called a sandy clay loam. Sandy clay loam is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One of the most important functions of soil in supporting plant growth is to provide essential plant nutrients: macro-nutrients and ____.
e: One of the most important functions of soil in supporting plant growth is to provide essential plant nutrients: macro-nutrients and micro-nutrients. Micro-nutrients is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Macro-nutrients are those elements that occur in ____ levels in plant materials or in fluids in the plant.
e: Macro-nutrients are those elements that occur in substantial levels in plant materials or in fluids in the plant. Substantial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Micro-nutrients are elements that are essential only at very low levels and generally are required for the functioning of ____.
e: Micro-nutrients are elements that are essential only at very low levels and generally are required for the functioning of enzymes. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions in cells.

q: Essential macro-nutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and ____.
e: Essential macro-nutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Essential micro-nutrients include boron, chlorine, copper, iron, manganese, molybdenum, zinc, sodium and ____.
e: Essential micro-nutrients include boron, chlorine, copper, iron, manganese, molybdenum, zinc, sodium and vanadium. Vanadium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (____) are plant nutrients that are obtained from soil.
e: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK) are plant nutrients that are obtained from soil. NPK is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are so important for crop productivity that they are commonly added to soil as ____.
e: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are so important for crop productivity that they are commonly added to soil as fertilisers. Fertilisers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen has the most dramatic effect on the ____ growth, especially in grass and cereal plants.
e: Nitrogen has the most dramatic effect on the leaf growth, especially in grass and cereal plants. Leaf is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen is used to make ____ in plants.
e: Nitrogen is used to make protein in plants. Protein is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nitrogen bound to soil ____ is especially important in maintaining soil fertility.
e: Nitrogen bound to soil humus is especially important in maintaining soil fertility. Humus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Phosphorus is essential in the ____ of every cell, so growth cannot continue in its complete absence.
e: Phosphorus is essential in the nucleus of every cell, so growth cannot continue in its complete absence. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system and ____ development.
e: Phosphorus is particularly associated with the development of a strong root system and floral development. Floral is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is required at high levels for growing plants.
e: Potassium is required at high levels for growing plants. Potassium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Potassium activates some enzymes and plays a key role in the ____ balance in plants.
e: Potassium activates some enzymes and plays a key role in the water balance in plants. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is a fundamental property that affects a surprisingly large range of chemical, physical and ____ processes in soils.
e: Soil pH is a fundamental property that affects a surprisingly large range of chemical, physical and biological processes in soils. Biological is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is a measure of the ____ and alkalinity in soils.
e: Soil pH is a measure of the acidity and alkalinity in soils. Acidity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The optimal pH range for most plants is between ____ and 7.0.
e: The optimal pH range for most plants is between 5.5 and 7.0. 5.5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil pH is important because of its effect on the ____ of essential elements, or nutrients, in soils.
e: Soil pH is important because of its effect on the availability of essential elements, or nutrients, in soils. Availability is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Many elements can be taken up by plants more easily if the soil pH is near neutral to marginally ____.
e: Many elements can be taken up by plants more easily if the soil pH is near neutral to marginally acidic. pH measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is, with 7 as neutral.

q: If the soil is more acidic than the required pH, it can be treated by adding ____.
e: If the soil is more acidic than the required pH, it can be treated by adding lime. Lime is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lime is ____ and it will neutralise the acidity of the soil and make it more neutral.
e: Lime is alkaline and it will neutralise the acidity of the soil and make it more neutral. Alkaline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Alkali or alkaline soils are clay soils with high pH (____).
e: Alkali or alkaline soils are clay soils with high pH (>8.5). >8.5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ helps in the treatment of alkaline soils.
e: Gypsum helps in the treatment of alkaline soils. Gypsum is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil is the receptor of large quantities of waste products: domestic, human, animal, industrial and ____ products.
e: Soil is the receptor of large quantities of waste products: domestic, human, animal, industrial and agricultural products. Agricultural is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Combustion of sulphur-containing fuels in the smelting process emits ____, and finally leaves sulphate on the soil.
e: Combustion of sulphur-containing fuels in the smelting process emits SO2, and finally leaves sulphate on the soil. SO2 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ from the atmosphere are deposited on the soil.
e: Nitrates from the atmosphere are deposited on the soil. Nitrates is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lead particulate from automobile exhausts settles on soil along both sides of highways with heavy automobile ____.
e: Lead particulate from automobile exhausts settles on soil along both sides of highways with heavy automobile traffic. Traffic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: High levels of Pb, Zn, etc. are observed on soils near lead and ____ mines.
e: High levels of Pb, Zn, etc. are observed on soils near lead and zinc mines. Zinc is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fertilisers and pesticides applied to crops are largely ____ by the soil.
e: Fertilisers and pesticides applied to crops are largely retained by the soil. Retained is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fertilisers and pesticides become part of environmental cycles due to sorption by the soil and ____ into water.
e: Fertilisers and pesticides become part of environmental cycles due to sorption by the soil and leaching into water. Leaching is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pesticides undergo degradation in soil through the processes of biodegradation, chemical degradation, or ____ reactions.
e: Pesticides undergo degradation in soil through the processes of biodegradation, chemical degradation, or photochemical reactions. Photochemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Insects, earthworms, plants and microorganisms play important roles in the ____ of pesticides.
e: Insects, earthworms, plants and microorganisms play important roles in the biodegradation of pesticides. Biodegradation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pesticide residues on crops and food products cause long-term ____.
e: Pesticide residues on crops and food products cause long-term health hazards. Health hazards is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The main sources which pollute the soil are acid rains, repeated or excess use of the same fertiliser, inadequate drainage system, and spraying plants with insecticides and ____.
e: The main sources which pollute the soil are acid rains, repeated or excess use of the same fertiliser, inadequate drainage system, and spraying plants with insecticides and herbicides. Herbicides is the idea that completes this fact.

q: ____ is the foundation of basic ecosystem function.
e: Soil is the foundation of basic ecosystem function. Soil is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Soil filters our water, provides essential nutrients to our forest and crops, and helps regulate the Earth's ____.
e: Soil filters our water, provides essential nutrients to our forest and crops, and helps regulate the Earth's temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact.
